Note::starts_with¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::starts_with(std::string_view prefix) const

Test Every Cell For A Literal Prefix¶

starts_with(prefix) reports, for each text cell, whether it begins with the literal string prefix. It is the anchored-at-the-start companion of contains: use it to route rows by a tag, a scheme, or a key prefix, when only a match at position 0 counts.

The test is a literal byte comparison — no regex, no case folding. Fold case first with lower for a case-insensitive check.

Return value¶

Like contains, the result is a Bool Note with the receiver’s shape: true where the cell starts with prefix, false otherwise. bools() exposes a borrowed contiguous host view when needed.

Edge cases¶

  • An empty prefix is a prefix of every cell, so every entry is 1.

  • A prefix longer than a cell cannot match: its entry is 0.

Example 1: Route By Prefix¶

const auto mask =
    pluss::make_note({"the end", "The end", "in the end"}).starts_with("the");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 0, 0]

Only the first cell starts with the exact bytes the; "The end" differs in case, and in "in the end" the match is not at position 0.

Example 2: An Empty Prefix Matches Everything¶

const auto mask = pluss::make_note({"x", ""}).starts_with("");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1]

Example 3: A Prefix Longer Than The Cell¶

const auto mask = pluss::make_note({"ab"}).starts_with("abcd");
std::cout << "[" << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[0]) << "]\n";

Output¶

[0]

Example 4: Higher-Rank Input Is Flattened Row-Major¶

const auto mask =
    pluss::make_note({{"img_1", "img_2"}, {"vid_1", "img_3"}}).starts_with("img_");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1, 0, 1]

See Also¶

  • Note::ends_with: the anchored-at-the-end counterpart.

  • Note::contains: match anywhere in the cell.

  • pluss::coden::Note::remove_prefix / ensure_prefix: act on the prefix rather than test for it.
